section_summary: This section documents U.S. Government and Allied occupation policy deliberations regarding the revival and control of Japanese economic recovery, foreign trade, and industrial capacity between May and July 1947. Key matters include the preparation of SWNCC 381, Allied debates within the Far Eastern Commission over disarmament and reparations from current output, raw material imports, and the Katayama Cabinet's emergency economic program and wage-price stabilization measures.

subfiles.about: Memorandum discussing implications of proposed State Department policy on Japanese economic recovery, occupation costs, and reparations.
subfiles.summary: Barnett analyzes complications of early treaty negotiations, repayment of occupation costs, Soviet claims for current reparations, and post-1950 export absorption.
subfiles.title: Further Remarks Regarding Promotion and Control of Japanese Economic Recovery

subfiles.about: Critique and proposed revisions of the draft SWNCC paper on Japanese economic recovery.
subfiles.summary: Walker critiques the draft SWNCC paper's narrow objectives, occupation withdrawal assumptions, projected $200 million export surplus, current reparations formulas, and non-convertible currency provisions.
subfiles.title: Draft SWNCC Paper on U.S. Policy with Respect to Promotion and Control of Japanese Economic Recovery

subfiles.about: Informal letter updating Bowman on Washington discussions concerning Japanese trade, cotton, and finance.
subfiles.summary: Whitman reports on IATB private trade quotas, cotton procurement disputes, Japanese textile limits, revolving fund clearances, and Indian trade negotiations.
subfiles.title: Letter to Dean O. Bowman Regarding Trade Policy and Economic Programs

subfiles.about: State Department reply regarding research materials on Japanese economic affairs.
subfiles.from: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Informs Professor Engle of the scope and coordination required to provide State Department materials for his Japanese economic research.
subfiles.title: Letter to Professor Nathanael H. Engle Regarding Research Materials on Japan

subfiles.about: Transmittal of Katayama Cabinet economic program and General MacArthur's letter to Yoshida.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the Katayama Cabinet's emergency economic program announced June 11, 1947, and General MacArthur's March 22 letter to Yoshida.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1112: Economic Program Announced by Japanese Government, June 11, 1947

subfiles.about: Japanese Government statement detailing eight emergency economic measures.
subfiles.summary: The Katayama Cabinet announces eight measures to stabilize the economy, focusing on food distribution, price adjustments, fiscal retrenchment, coal production, labor security, export promotion, and key enterprise control.
subfiles.title: Emergency Economic Measures

subfiles.about: Letter from MacArthur directing the Japanese Government to implement comprehensive economic controls.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur emphasizes Japanese Government responsibility for food rationing and prices, warning that Allied aid requires full domestic mobilization and effective controls.
subfiles.title: Letter to Prime Minister Shigeru Yoshida Regarding Economic Stabilization

subfiles.about: Form designating replacement record copy for telegram 894.50/6-1847.
subfiles.summary: Official form designating replacement record copy for telegram 894.50/6-1847.
subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Form for Telegram 894.50/6-1847

subfiles.about: Military operational report covering Japanese livestock slaughter, labor education, and Diet affairs.
subfiles.summary: Reports March-April livestock slaughter statistics, trade union education attendance, radio frequency additions, Diet recess extension, and appointment of parliamentary vice-ministers.
subfiles.title: Incoming Telegram Z-11003 (Section 2 Operations Report Japan)

subfiles.about: Form designating replacement record copy for Despatch 1545 from London.
subfiles.summary: Official form designating replacement record copy for London Despatch 1545.
subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Form for Despatch 1545 from London

subfiles.about: Transmittal of Manchester Guardian article reflecting Australian views on Japan's future.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a Manchester Guardian article reporting Australian concerns that U.S. rehabilitation of Japan could threaten Australia's economic position.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1545: Transmitting Article from Manchester Guardian on Australian View of Future of Japan

subfiles.about: Letter introducing J. Meyer Friedman to discuss Japanese operations.
subfiles.summary: Introduces J. Meyer Friedman, requesting an appointment with George McGhee regarding commercial operations in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter Introducing J. Meyer Friedman

subfiles.about: Reply offering to refer J. Meyer Friedman to State Department officials.
subfiles.summary: McGhee offers to refer Friedman to John Carter Vincent or Edwin M. Martin for guidance on Japanese business matters.
subfiles.title: Letter Regarding Introduction of J. Meyer Friedman

subfiles.about: Memorandum proposing specific drafting changes to the revised SWNCC paper on Japanese economic revival.
subfiles.summary: Tyson suggests wording revisions to highlight private financing, limit U.S. appropriations, clarify export surplus prerequisites, and qualify occupation cost repayment clauses.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Proposed SWNCC Paper on the Revival of the Japanese Economy

subfiles.about: Attached fragment of May 21 memorandum commenting on the draft SWNCC recovery paper.
subfiles.summary: Incomplete copy of Walker's May 21 memorandum attached to Tyson's memorandum, discussing recovery objectives and occupation withdrawal issues.
subfiles.title: Attachment: Memorandum on Draft SWNCC Paper on Promotion and Control of Japanese Economic Recovery (Fragment)

subfiles.about: Report on Chinese consideration of a foreign exchange link system for exporters.
subfiles.summary: Reports that the proposal allowing Chinese exporters to retain exchange for imports was referred back to the Central Bank.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1683 from Shanghai on Proposed Chinese Link System

subfiles.about: Transmittal of approved working-level answers to Chinese questions on FEC 084/12.
subfiles.summary: Transmits approved State Department working-level answers for Blakeslee's use in replying to Chinese queries in the FEC Steering Committee.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on U.S. Reply to Chinese Member Regarding Paragraph 9(b) of FEC 084/12

subfiles.about: Formal U.S. answers to questions raised by the Chinese member regarding industrial capacities and reparations.
subfiles.from: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.summary: Answers ten Chinese questions, clarifying the January 1, 1949 date, lack of precise operating capacity data, SCAP authority, and current-account reparations.
subfiles.title: Answers to Questions Posed by the Chinese Member Regarding U.S. Amendment to Paragraph 9(b) of FEC 084/12

subfiles.about: Urgent note routing revised draft answers for the FEC Steering Committee meeting.
subfiles.summary: Urgent note sending revised answers drafted by Barnett and cleared by NA to Blakeslee for reproduction.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip Transmitting Draft Answers on FEC 084/12

subfiles.about: Draft responses to Chinese questions concerning Japanese industrial capacity and FEC 084/12.
subfiles.summary: Draft text detailing U.S. positions on FEC 218 capacity levels, SCAP plant designations, disarmament agreements, post-1949 additions, and reparations.
subfiles.title: Draft Reply to Questions Posed by the Chinese Member Regarding U.S. Amendment to Paragraph 9(b) of FEC 084/12

subfiles.about: Academic request for copies of the Japanese economic white paper.
subfiles.summary: Professor Harris requests copies of the Japanese Government's white paper on the Japanese economic situation.
subfiles.title: Letter Requesting White Paper on Japanese Economic Situation

subfiles.about: State Department response regarding the availability of the Japanese economic white paper.
subfiles.summary: Martin informs Harris that the 100-page white paper is being obtained from Tokyo, enclosing the seven-page Japanese program release and MacArthur letter.
subfiles.title: Letter Regarding Availability of Japanese Economic White Paper

subfiles.about: Form designating replacement record copy for Despatch 1180 from Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Official form designating replacement record copy for Tokyo Despatch 1180.
subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Form for Despatch 1180 from Tokyo

subfiles.about: Report transmitting Japanese economic statements, white paper, wage policy, and editorial comment.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the Katayama Cabinet's economic policy statement, the July 4 white paper, the July 5 wage-price statement, and Japanese press editorial summaries.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1180: Economic Policy Statements of the Japanese Government

subfiles.about: English translation of the Katayama Cabinet's eight-point emergency economic program.
subfiles.summary: Official translation of the Katayama Cabinet's program addressing food distribution, price-wage revision, fiscal austerity, production priority, labor protection, export expansion, and key enterprise control.
subfiles.title: Emergency Economic Measures (Translation)

subfiles.about: Statement explaining government decision to fix average monthly wages at 1,800 yen.
subfiles.summary: The Economic Stabilization Board justifies fixing industrial average wages at 1,800 yen and rejecting the 2,400 yen union demand to prevent runaway inflation.
subfiles.title: Draft of Government's Statement on Stabilization of Wages and Prices

subfiles.about: Summary of Tokyo newspaper editorials concerning the government's economic white paper.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes editorials from Yomiuri, Jiji, Mainichi, Nippon Keizai, and Asahi commenting on the Katayama Cabinet's economic white paper.
subfiles.title: A Consensus of Editorial Comment Published July 5, 1947 on the Japanese Government's "White Paper", Issued July 4, 1947

subfiles.about: Recommendation to appoint a War Department expediter to coordinate the Japanese recovery program.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring recommends appointing a high-level executive expediter to coordinate U.S. operations for Japanese economic self-support under SWNCC 381.
subfiles.title: Letter to Howard C. Petersen Regarding Appointment of a War Department Expediter

subfiles.about: Transmittal of State Department policy paper on Japanese economic revival to SWNCC.
subfiles.summary: Submits the State Department's proposed policy paper, "Revival of the Japanese Economy," to SWNCC for referral to the Subcommittee for the Far East.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for the Secretary, SWNCC: Proposed SWNCC Paper on the Revival of the Japanese Economy

subfiles.about: Instruction transmitting copy of SWNCC 381 to the Political Adviser in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a copy of SWNCC 381, "Revival of the Japanese Economy," to the U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo for information.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 535 Transmitting SWNCC 381, "Revival of the Japanese Economy"
